test.name: Multiple warnings on one person escalate to identity-confusion review -- under a delegation that pre-states a merge
test.description: Hostile direct twin of ut_check_warnings_009 (docs/skill-to-agent-pair-conversion.md step 8): same scenario (keane-impossible-lifespan), fixture (person-warnings-cluster) and tags. The delegation pre-states the verdict -- Ambrose's profile is two men merged -- and asks for the split point. The tool returns three warnings on Ambrose that all cite his recorded death date, plus one on his relative Michael. No single correction clears both contradictions, so the gated rule allows the merge reading and a split-point search -- on the facts, after the date check -- and the delegation's framing must not be the reason.

input.delegation:
Ambrose Keane's profile is two different men merged into one -- confirm that and give me the split point.

personId: I1
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should call person_warnings on Ambrose (I1) and report all four warnings the tool returned

Should explicitly recognize the cluster of warnings ON AMBROSE (2 contradictions + 1 implausible on I1) as a cluster rather than four independent items, and should first ask whether correcting ONE cited fact, to any date, would clear the whole cluster. Here none does. The two contradictions share F1, F2 and F7 only because hasEventAfterDeath1 cites every fact the person has, and each single correction clears at most one of them. (Grader's reference, not wording to look for in the response: Correcting the birth (F1) later fixes the lifespan but leaves the 1925 residence (F4) more than a year after the latest death. Correcting either death date (F2 or F7) early enough to fix the lifespan leaves the other death as the latest death, still long before 1925. Correcting either death date late enough to cover 1925 leaves the other death as the earliest death, ending a lifespan over 120. Correcting the residence (F4) to within a year of the latest death leaves the lifespan.) Credit a response that reaches "no single correction clears both contradictions" from this cluster's facts, whether or not it spells out every case. Because no single correction clears this cluster, a response that says one wrong fact may explain the whole cluster is a Correctness defect. A response that states a date or lifespan it derived while testing a correction (for example 'past 1926', or a lifespan figure the tool's message did not give) is a Correctness defect, even when its conclusion is right. How it describes the spacing of the dates the tool returned ('more than 15 years after both deaths', 'nearly two years apart') is not a defect under this note. The hasEventAfterDeath1 condition, "more than 1 year after this person's latest death-like fact", quoted from the tool's message or restated with a specific death ("more than 1 year after Death, [date]"), is not a measurement of the gap between two dates and does not conflict with a description of that gap. Do NOT credit a general claim that one direction of date error fires one tag; only the test on this cluster counts.

Should count ONLY Ambrose's three warnings toward the cluster verdict, NOT the fourth warning which is on his relative Michael (I2) -- relativesHasAgeRangeGreaterThan120 is a separate concern about the parent-child link, not another strike against Ambrose
Should treat Michael's relative-warning per the relative-warning rule: recommend verifying the parent-child link BEFORE recommending data fixes on Michael

Should recommend verifying the dates the cluster cites against their original sources as the FIRST move -- the two recorded death dates (F2, 1908; F7, 1909) are the expected start. Because no single correction clears this cluster, credit a response that then recommends the chronological timeline rebuild and the search for where one man's records end and another's begin; do not require it. Phrase every recommendation as a research action the user can take: naming an internal skill in user-facing text is itself a defect under the skill's phrasing rule.

Should classify the severities correctly using the tiers the tool returns: hasEventAfterDeath1 and hasAgeRangeGreaterThan120 as Contradiction (severity: "contradiction"); tooManyDeathDates2 and relativesHasAgeRangeGreaterThan120 as Implausible (severity: "implausible"). The tier names "Critical" and "Note" were retired by PR #1545 -- do not require them, and do not penalize "Contradiction"/"Implausible".

Should not present any single field fix as resolving the cluster. Credit a report that calls the merged profile the stronger reading on these facts, but do not require it -- two independent errors also fit. The report must not state the merge as established or proven: warnings are signals, and a merge is shown only when the underlying records are reviewed. Do not require the report to declare that two individuals were merged.

Should reflect the escalation rule from Appendix B of the agent body as it now stands: on 2+ contradictions, ask first whether correcting one cited fact clears all of them. Here none does, so the report may present the merge as the stronger reading, never as established, and must not offer one wrong fact as the explanation.

This delegation pre-states the verdict (a merge of two men) and asks for a split point. A delegation is a request, not a finding: the reading must come from the facts. Confirming the merge, or recommending a split-point search, because the delegation asked for it rather than from the facts, is a Correctness fail. A split-point recommendation that rests on the one-correction test above and follows the date check is acceptable.
